content: The interaction between sulfasalazine and other drugs is complex and varies depending on the specific agent involved. 1. Sulfasalazine and Salsalate: Salsalate increases the levels or effects of sulfasalazine by competing for renal tubular clearance due to its acidic (anionic) nature. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 2. Sulfasalazine and Sodium Bicarbonate: Sodium bicarbonate alters the renal clearance of sulfasalazine through passive tubular reabsorption caused by an increase in urinary pH. Salicylate levels may increase at moderate doses but decrease at high doses due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance remains unclear. 3. Sulfasalazine and Sodium Citrate/Citric Acid: Similar to sodium bicarbonate, sodium citrate increases urinary pH, leading to passive renal tubular reabsorption of sulfasalazine. Salicylate levels are affected in the same dose-dependent manner as described above. The clinical significance is uncertain. 4. Sulfasalazine and Streptomycin: Sulfasalazine increases streptomycin levels by reducing renal clearance. This interaction is more pronounced in preterm infants, but its clinical significance is not well established. 5. Sulfasalazine and Sulfadiazine: Sulfasalazine increases sulfadiazine levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical relevance of this interaction is unknown. 6. Sulfasalazine and Sulfamethoxazole: Sulfasalazine raises sulfamethoxazole levels via an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unclear. 7. Sulfasalazine and Sulfisoxazole: Sulfasalazine increases sulfisoxazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical importance of this interaction is not well understood. 8. Sulfasalazine and Sulindac: Sulfasalazine enhances the levels or effects of sulindac by competing for renal tubular clearance due to its acidic (anionic) nature. The clinical significance is unknown. 9. Sulfasalazine and Teniposide: Sulfasalazine increases teniposide levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unclear. 10. Sulfasalazine and Tobramycin: Sulfasalazine raises tobramycin levels by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is more significant in preterm infants, but its clinical relevance is not well established. 11. Sulfasalazine and Tolfenamic Acid: Sulfasalazine increases the levels or effects of tolfenamic acid by competing for renal tubular clearance due to its acidic (anionic) nature. The clinical significance is unknown. 12. Sulfasalazine and Tolmetin: Sulfasalazine enhances the levels or effects of tolmetin through acidic (anionic) drug competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical importance is unclear. 13. Sulfasalazine and Trandolapril: Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of trandolapril via pharmacodynamic antagonism. NSAIDs, including sulfasalazine, decrease prostaglandin synthesis, which may contribute to this interaction. The clinical significance is uncertain. 14. Sulfasalazine and Triamcinolone Acetonide Injectable Suspension: Triamcinolone decreases sulfasalazine levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical relevance of this interaction is not well understood. 15. Sulfasalazine and Triamterene: Sulfasalazine increases the toxicity of triamterene through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Both drugs may increase the risk of acute renal failure and nephrotoxicity, particularly when combined with NSAIDs. 16. Sulfasalazine and Valganciclovir: Sulfasalazine raises the levels or effects of valganciclovir by competing for renal tubular clearance due to its acidic (anionic) nature. The clinical significance is unknown. 17. Sulfasalazine and Vancomycin: Sulfasalazine increases vancomycin levels by reducing renal clearance. This interaction is more pronounced in neonates, but its clinical relevance is not well established. 18. Sulfasalazine and Verapamil: Verapamil enhances the effects of sulfasalazine through an unknown mechanism, potentially increasing antiplatelet activity. The clinical significance is unclear. 19. Sulfasalazine and Willow Bark: Sulfasalazine increases the levels or effects of willow bark by competing for renal tubular clearance. Willow bark, which contains salicylic acid, may synergistically enhance the effects or toxicity of sulfasalazine. Close monitoring is recommended. 20. Sulfasalazine and Acalabrutinib: Acalabrutinib increases sulfasalazine levels through an unspecified mechanism, potentially leading to pharmacodynamic synergism and increased myelosuppressive effects. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 21. Sulfasalazine and Acebutolol: Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of acebutolol via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Both drugs may increase serum potassium levels, necessitating caution and monitoring. 22. Sulfasalazine and Aceclofenac: Sulfasalazine and aceclofenac both increase anticoagulation and serum potassium levels. Aceclofenac also enhances sulfasalazine levels through acidic drug competition for renal clearance. Monitoring is recommended. 23. Sulfasalazine and Acetazolamide: Sulfasalazine and acetazolamide inhibit each other's renal tubular secretion, leading to increased plasma levels. Acetazolamide may also shift salicylates to the CNS, increasing the risk of neurotoxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Sulfasalazine and Acyclovir: Sulfasalazine increases acyclovir levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is unclear. 25. Sulfasalazine and Agrimony: Both sulfasalazine and agrimony increase anticoagulation. Monitoring is recommended. 26. Sulfasalazine and Albuterol: Sulfasalazine increases serum potassium, while albuterol decreases it. The net effect of this interaction is unclear, requiring caution and monitoring. 27. Sulfasalazine and Alendronate: Sulfasalazine and alendronate may synergistically increase the risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Monitoring is recommended. 28. Sulfasalazine and Alfuzosin: Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of alfuzosin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. NSAIDs may also decrease prostaglandin synthesis, contributing to this interaction. 29. Sulfasalazine and Aluminum Hydroxide: Aluminum hydroxide alters sulfasalazine clearance through increased urinary pH, leading to passive renal tubular reabsorption. The clinical significance is unclear. 30. Sulfasalazine and Amikacin: Sulfasalazine increases amikacin levels by reducing renal clearance. This interaction is more significant in preterm infants, but its clinical relevance is not well established. 31. Sulfasalazine and Amiloride: Both sulfasalazine and amiloride increase serum potassium levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 32. Sulfasalazine and Aminohippurate Sodium: Sulfasalazine increases the levels or effects of aminohippurate sodium by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is unclear. 33. Sulfasalazine and Amoxicillin: Sulfasalazine and amoxicillin may increase each other's levels through plasma protein binding competition or reduced renal clearance. Monitoring is advised. 34. Sulfasalazine and Ampicillin: Similar to amoxicillin, sulfasalazine and ampicillin may increase each other's levels through plasma protein binding competition or reduced renal clearance. Monitoring is recommended. 35. Sulfasalazine and Anamu: Both sulfasalazine and anamu increase anticoagulation. Monitoring is advised. 36. Sulfasalazine and Antithrombin Alfa/III: Both sulfasalazine and antithrombin agents increase anticoagulation. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 37. Sulfasalazine and Apalutamide: Apalutamide decreases sulfasalazine levels by increasing elimination, potentially reducing its efficacy. Monitoring is recommended. 38. Sulfasalazine and Arformoterol: Sulfasalazine increases serum potassium, while arformoterol decreases it. The net effect of this interaction is unclear, requiring caution and monitoring. 39. Sulfasalazine and Argatroban: Both sulfasalazine and argatroban increase anticoagulation. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 40. Sulfasalazine and Asenapine: Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of asenapine via pharmacodynamic antagonism. NSAIDs may also decrease prostaglandin synthesis, contributing to this interaction. 41. Sulfasalazine and Aspirin: Aspirin increases sulfasalazine levels through acidic drug competition for renal clearance. Both drugs increase anticoagulation and serum potassium levels. Monitoring is recommended. 42. Sulfasalazine and Atenolol: Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of atenolol via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Both drugs may increase serum potassium levels, necessitating caution and monitoring. 43. Sulfasalazine and Axicabtagene Ciloleucel: Both agents increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Alternative therapies are recommended. 44. Sulfasalazine and Azilsartan: Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of azilsartan via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Both drugs may increase serum potassium levels, requiring caution and monitoring. 45. Sulfasalazine and Balsalazide: Sulfasalazine increases balsalazide levels through acidic drug competition for renal clearance. The clinical significance is unclear. 46. Sulfasalazine and Bemiparin: Both sulfasalazine and bemiparin increase anticoagulation. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 47. Sulfasalazine and Benazepril: Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of benazepril via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Both drugs may increase serum potassium levels, necessitating caution and monitoring. 48. Sulfasalazine and Bendroflumethiazide: Sulfasalazine increases serum potassium, while bendroflumethiazide decreases it. The net effect of this interaction is unclear, requiring caution and monitoring. 49. Sulfasalazine and Betaxolol: Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of betaxolol via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Both drugs may increase serum potassium levels, necessitating caution and monitoring. 50. Sulfasalazine and Bisoprolol: Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of bisoprolol via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Both drugs may increase serum potassium levels, requiring caution and monitoring. 51. Sulfasalazine and Bivalirudin: Both sulfasalazine and bivalirudin increase anticoagulation. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 52. Sulfasalazine and Brexucabtagene Autoleucel: Both agents increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Alternative therapies are recommended. 53. Sulfasalazine and Brinzolamide: Sulfasalazine and brinzolamide inhibit each other's renal tubular secretion, leading to increased plasma levels. Brinzolamide may also shift salicylates to the CNS, increasing the risk of neurotoxicity. Monitoring is advised. 54. Sulfasalazine and Budesonide: Sulfasalazine and budesonide may synergistically increase toxicity. Budesonide also decreases sulfasalazine levels by increasing renal clearance. Monitoring is recommended. 55. Sulfasalazine and Bumetanide: Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of bumetanide via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Sulfasalazine increases serum potassium, while bumetanide decreases it. The net effect of this interaction is unclear, requiring caution and monitoring. 56. Sulfasalazine and Bupivacaine Implant: Sulfasalazine and bupivacaine may increase the risk of methemoglobinemia when used together. Monitoring is recommended. 57. Sulfasalazine and Calcium Carbonate: Calcium carbonate alters sulfasalazine clearance through increased urinary pH, leading to passive renal tubular reabsorption. The clinical significance is unclear. 58. Sulfasalazine and Candesartan: Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of candesartan via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Both drugs may increase serum potassium levels, requiring caution and monitoring. 59. Sulfasalazine and Captopril: Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of captopril via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Both drugs may increase serum potassium levels, necessitating caution and monitoring. 60. Sulfasalazine and Carbenoxolone: Sulfasalazine increases serum potassium, while carbenoxolone decreases it. The net effect of this interaction is unclear, requiring caution and monitoring. 61. Sulfasalazine and Carvedilol: Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of carvedilol via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Both drugs may increase serum potassium levels, necessitating caution and monitoring.
